answer.rationale: Write-path p99 degradation began within the window following a release, making rollback_release the most directly evidenced fix (memory_b1: rollback cleared a similar checkout error spike cleanly). Regional_failover is explicitly contraindicated here: memory_b2 warns never to fail over while writes are hot, and we are at daily settlement peak with heavy writes, so that action risks a replication gap and lost customer writes despite fast latency recovery historically. Add_capacity (b3) and read-replica routing (b5) address load/read pressure, not a release-correlated write-path regression, and circuit breakers (b4) are suited to a partner-dependency failure mode, not this symptom set. I verify b1 and b2 because they are the two candidate actions most directly implicated by current symptoms and because b2 carries an explicit safety warning that must be confirmed before ruling failover out. Given the release-timing correlation is suggestive but not proven (peak load alone could also explain the climb), I stage the rollback as a guarded, closely monitored action rather than a full broad rollout, so impact can be assessed quickly and the next window can pivot to add_capacity or read-replica routing if latency doesn't recover.
